elements.element: Customer owns every Deliverable created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly provides that “Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer.”

elements.element: Vendor presently assigns every Deliverable created for Customer to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 states that Vendor “hereby assigns” each such Deliverable to Customer.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause grants ownership only of defined “Deliverables”; it does not mention work product or establish that all work product is included within Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor presently assigns all work product created for Customer to Customer.
elements.evidence: The present assignment applies only to each Deliverable. There is no assignment of work product that may fall outside that term.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 states that Vendor retains “Vendor Technology,” but the supplied language does not define that term or expressly confirm that it includes all Vendor pre-existing intellectual property.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to any Vendor intellectual property embedded in a Deliverable.
elements.evidence: Sections 14.3 and 13.2 grant Customer a licence to Vendor Technology incorporated in, required to use, or embedded in a Deliverable.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in a Deliverable is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable licence perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in a Deliverable is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable licence irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in a Deliverable is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable licence royalty-free and fully paid.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 states that Customer owns all Customer Data and that no right transfers to Vendor other than a limited processing right for specified purposes.

elements.element: No jointly owned intellectual property is created.
elements.evidence: Section 14.4 provides that no jointly owned intellectual property is created under the clause. Its exception requires a separate signed instrument, which would independently establish any future joint ownership.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The clause says Vendor retains Vendor Technology, but it does not expressly identify generic tools as Vendor-owned or establish that generic tools are included within Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: The operative language does not address ownership of Vendor know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to use the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Customer owns the Deliverables under Section 14.2, but the clause does not grant Customer a licence to the Deliverables. Section 13.2 licenses only software and Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer's licence to the Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: No licence to the Deliverables is granted. The perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies only to software and Vendor Technology, although Customer's ownership rights in Deliverables are not term-limited.

elements.element: Customer's licence to the Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No licence to the Deliverables is granted; the irrevocability language applies only to the Section 13.2 licence for software and Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer's licence to the Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: No licence to the Deliverables is granted; the worldwide scope in Section 13.2 applies only to software and Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer's licence to the Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No licence to the Deliverables is granted; the royalty-free language in Section 13.2 applies only to software and Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer's licence permits modification of the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 permits modification of licensed software and Vendor Technology, but there is no express licence permitting modification of the Deliverables themselves.

elements.element: Customer's licence permits sublicensing of the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No Deliverable licence or sublicensing right is stated. Section 13.2 only permits contractors to support licensed material and does not grant a general sublicensing right.

elements.element: Customer's licence permits use of the Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The “for Customer's business” limitation appears only in the Section 13.2 licence for software and Vendor Technology, not in a licence to the Deliverables.

result.reason: The redline clearly reverses Deliverable ownership and supplies a present assignment while preserving Customer Data ownership, embedded Vendor Technology licensing, and the prohibition on automatic joint ownership. However, it omits ownership and assignment of work product outside “Deliverables” and does not expressly preserve all pre-existing Vendor IP. It also does not implement the fallback's express ownership of generic tools and know-how or its Deliverable licence structure. The changes otherwise preserve the surrounding commercial terms without an apparent contradiction.
